# How can this retained developmental capacity be exploited in plant tissue culture and genetic engineering?

The carrot culture shows that specialised cells are usually stable but not permanently locked into one developmental state.

Under controlled laboratory conditions, some mature cells can return to division and later form every tissue of a new plant.

This makes it possible to multiply valuable plants from tiny tissue samples and to modify dividing cells before they specialise again.

How can scientists use this controlled developmental flexibility to produce disease-resistant crops on a large scale?
